full_judgment:
4. Being aggrieved by the judgment of the learned Subordinate Judge, the Defendants (heirs of original Defendant no. 1) preferred an appeal. The learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court allowed, the appeal and dismissed the suit giving his own reasoning’s. He found that the lease by Abdul Aziz in favour of Hazi Abdus Sattar by Kobulyat Ext A and subsequent Kabuliyats as alleged by the Defendants were true and genuine and they were acted upon. Although there was no Patta made in pursuance of Kabuliat or any rent receipt produced by the Defendants, the learned Additional District Judge observed:- 

 5. The learned Additional District Judge noticed that there was a recital in the kabala Ext 2c about the registered kabuliyat Ext A and also unregistered kobulyats executed by Abdus Sattar in favour of Hazi Azizullah. Thereafter, the learned Additional District Judge considered the factum of possession. In doing so, he noticed that the three kabalas of the Plaintiffs Ext 2-2(b) related only to Plot No. 950 and in the plaint, there was an explanation that the boundary given in the kabalas would attract the lands of plot No. 951, while the Defendants claimed to have four residential huts upon the plot No. 951. The learned Additional District Judge, on the prayer of the Defendant, allowed local inspection and passed his finding of possession mainly upon the report of the commissioner. In substance, he found that the huts of the Defendants were found in plot No. 951 and plot 950 was a vacant land. The learned Additional District Judge, amongst others things, was of the opinion that "In our country, it is very often found, rather it is very natural, that after the death of any daughter or female folk, her heirs lose all connection with her paternal family. When wife of Syed Moula Ali died 18/19 years ago no man can believe that heirs of Syed Moula Ali had any connection with the family or that late Abdus Sattar, not to speak of taking any usufruct from the suit land when the suit property along with other property were undivided throughout."
